handback.t:
All six docs are written, committed and pushed to origin (master, 153cbe3), but the pipeline numbers and market figures are unverified. WebSearch had hit its 200-call budget before I started, so I did no new research. Every external fact, competitor description and firm thesis is grade C or "verify" and says so.

**Files written** (in `C:\Users\mariu\ventures\subrogation-recovery`):
- `business/business-plan.md`, `business/market-analysis.md`
- `financial/model.md`
- `technical/overview.md`
- `fundraising/README.md`, `hiring/README.md`
- one-line index READMEs for business, financial and technical
- the report at `scratchpad\build-subro-docs.md`

**Contents**
- **#1 milestone (G0):** validate the real missed-recovery rate on one carrier's closed files before building further. The plan sets a blind-review protocol of at least 1,000 files, go at 0.3% or more of paid losses as net incremental collectible, and stop below 0.15%. Both thresholds are assumptions I set, to be fixed before looking at data.
- **The headline figures:**
  - **$15-20B missed per year:** flagged as grade C, weak, unvalidated.
  - **$51.6B recovered in 2021:** grade C, second-hand.
- **Market analysis:** a competitor teardown covering CLARA Analytics, Verisk, SubroIQ, the claims-platform vendors, law firms, recovery vendors and Arbitration Forums. It lays out why execution rather than detection is the wedge, and treats Guidewire, CCC, Mitchell, Verisk, Sedgwick and Crawford as speculative acquirers.
- **Model:** contingency unit economics per carrier account (base ACV $150K, 20% fee, CAC payback about 22-24 months). It also flags the "lookback harvest" that inflates early revenue and the problem of agreeing a baseline for incremental contingency fees.
- **Five-year build, year-5 run-rate:**

  | Scenario | Run-rate | Value at 8-15x ARR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Base | $10.5M | $84-158M |
  | Bull | $37.5M | $300-563M |
  | Bear | $0.9M | not meaningful |

  - **Capital:** seed $3.0-3.5M; about $16M, $56M and $2M of total capital for base, bull and bear.
- **$1B:** stated explicitly that no scenario credibly reaches it, including bull. It would take about 270-500 accounts at $250K, or about 70-125 large carriers at about $1M each. That would mean roughly 17-22% of the whole fee pool if the vendor figure is only a third real.
- **Fundraising:** insurtech and fintech VCs, corporate venture arms, a Nordic section (Antler, Alliance Venture, Investinor, Northzone, Creandum, Maki.vc, Innovation Norway, SkatteFUNN), and 2 outreach templates. All firm-level and official channels only; none of the firms was re-verified, so check each on its own site before outreach.
- **Hiring:** a Norway-based operator/CEO option, a subrogation domain lead, a founding engineer, and an integrations engineer. Sourcing is via recruiters and official channels, with no named individuals.

**Things to know**
- **Code appeared mid-run.** `src/subrogation_recovery/` (about 1,150 lines of Python, Dockerfile, CI, fixtures) was added by something else while I worked; I started from a docs-only repo. My first `git add -A` commit (966aca7, 44 files) swept in that code and pushed it. I then rewrote section 0 of `technical/overview.md` to match what the code does. The state tables cover only 13 states and are unreviewed by counsel; it has no verifier and no LLM provider yet.
- **Tests:** I counted 25 test functions but did not run them, because pytest isn't installed and I didn't install anything.
- **Left untracked:** `tests/*.py` and a `deploy/` folder, which belong to that other work.
- **Edits since I read the files:** three files (`fundraising/README.md`, `technical/overview.md`, `business/business-plan.md`) showed as changed on disk after I last read them. They are presumably from the parallel process; I took them as current and did not revert them.
